title: Run boundary scan in producer and on request input at admission
summary: Two changes so banned boundary words are caught early: the producer brief tells it to run `cargo test -p xtask --test policy` on its changes and fix findings before finishing, and Athena scans the request text and any files it names with the same scan before admitting the job, so a hit is reworded first. Audience: the user and the verifier, who saw job a5sf fail on a word in docs/design/job-planning.md.

defaults_applied.how: New tests for brief text, request scan, and named-file scan; cargo test and clippy pass.
Criteria run the scan on planted words and check flagging happens.
The scan is enforced at admission by code, not prose only.
Fixes the gap that input and brief word lists alone let a banned word through.
Changelog and comments written for outside readers.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: `Admits the job` means the intake step before a producer is dispatched, not the post-change admission in admission.rs; the hook goes where the request is first handled (likely run/mod.rs).
Reword-first means Athena reports the hit and the request is not admitted until reworded; it does not silently edit the user's text.
The producer's ability to run cargo test is already allowed; this change only adds the instruction to the brief.
docs/design/job-planning.md may still need rewording if it fails the scan on this branch.

acceptance_criteria.text: The producer brief built in crates/athena-context/src/briefs.rs tells the producer to run `cargo test -p xtask --test policy` on its changed files before finishing and to reword any banned word found; a unit test asserts this text is in the producer brief.

A new test shows a request text containing a banned boundary word (built from fragments) is flagged before admission with the word and its location, while a clean request passes. Run `cargo test` and see the test pass.
A new test shows a file named in the request that contains a banned word is flagged before admission, with its path and line, and a clean named file is not. Run `cargo test`.

Admission-time scanning reuses the same word list as the policy scan (boundary_words/boundary_fragments or a shared source), not a third copy; the existing test that keeps the brief list equal to the scanner list still passes.
`cargo test --locked` passes in full, including athena_refers_to_no_one_who_runs_it_or_where, and `cargo clippy` is clean; no new tracked file contains a banned word.
CHANGELOG.md notes the new behavior in plain language for an outside reader.

out_of_scope: Rewriting the scan in policy.rs beyond exposing it for reuse
Automatic editing of user request text
departures: Touches both the brief and the intake path, so a bit above the reference cost and time.
urgent_reason: Cuts failed and rejected attempts like job a5sf, where a banned word was only found in verification.
hard_reason: Changes the admission gate that judges other jobs, so a mistake is costly.
